newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit in range ahead of U.S. payrolls report.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit in range ahead of U.S. payrolls report.

text.p: The ringgit was kept in a tight range in Asian trading on Friday due to lack of fresh leads, dealers said.
Market participants were largely sidelined ahead of the weekend and release of U.S. non-farm payrolls report at 1230 GMT, they said.
Dealers said the ringgit was unlikely to move very much later in London or New York.
"Unless there is a big surprise in the U.S. jobs report, the ringgit should stay rangebound," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
U.S. non-farm payrolls were expected to show a rise of 211,000 in April against 175,000 in March.

Dealers said the ringgit showed some movements in late trading as some American banks sold some of their dollar/ringgit positions ahead of the report. "This took the ringgit to 2.5080 (a dollar)," one dealer said.
Dealers said the ringgit was trying to hold below 2.5100 a dollar after breaking through the level on Wednesday. The Kuala Lumpur market was closed on Thursday for Labour Day.
At 0150 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5078/88 a dollar.
